references.text: Here the use of the onyx stones (שֹׁהַם) on the ephod is described, where the names of the twelve tribes of Israel were to be engraved
Detailed description of the set stones (אַבְנֵי מִלֻּאִים) that were to be placed on the breastpiece (חֹשֶׁן)
Introduction of the ephod (אֵפֹד) and the breastpiece (חֹשֶׁן) as parts of the high priest's garments
Repetition of the gathering of onyx stones and setting stones for the ephod and the breastpiece
The leaders brought onyx stones and setting stones for the ephod and the breastpiece
The execution of the work with the onyx stones that were set on the ephod
The execution of the work with the set stones on the breastpiece
First mention of the onyx stone (שֹׁהַם) in the Bible, in the description of Eden
David gathered onyx stones and setting stones for the temple
Explains how the onyx stone from 25:7 was actually set and placed on the breastpiece.
Confirms that the requirement for the onyx stone in 25:7 was fulfilled exactly as God instructed.
